title: Picking with two fingers for volume and tone
summary: Foster picks with the first two fingers together for volume and grips the strings for tone.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So little form. So little form. So, you know, I'm going to ask, which fingers you pick with, do you pick with two fingers together? Both the first and second, usually.
Do you pick sometimes one at a time or both together?
No, both together all the time.
All the time. More volume. Both together, get more volume.

Volume, and I, grip, because I, see, grip and electric guitar. You got to grip those strings to get your tonation. Your tonation is up there. That's what he taught me. That's what I've been doing. You know? It's like, you say, man, finger by, you take a big bar, finger by, and if I do that, I don't get no tones together.
Yeah. That's a grip of tight to hold it down firm. I know that.

You get tone, see? Mm-hmm. You know? And I try as a player doing it just like my aunt tell me. When you make a change, you can hear it out there, and if you make a blue note, you can hear it out there. That's right. See? Right. That one may let be a good one. See? Mm-hmm. Well done. And sometimes you make them, you try to catch them. You know? You do it in a minute. It's like, oh, it's gone. Right.
